methods.name: agrestiCoull
methods.signature: agrestiCoull(k: number, n: number, z = Z95): Interval
methods.definition: Agresti-Coull: n~ = n + z^2, p~ = (k + z^2 / 2) / n~, p~ -/+ z sqrt(p~ (1 - p~) / n~), clipped to [0, 1]; estimate k / n
methods.source: Agresti and Coull 1998; Brown, Cai and DasGupta 2001 (binomial proportion confidence interval, dossier S8)

methods.name: jeffreys
methods.signature: jeffreys(k: number, n: number, alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Jeffreys: Beta(k + 1/2, n - k + 1/2) quantiles at alpha / 2 and 1 - alpha / 2; lower 0 when k = 0, upper 1 when k = n
methods.source: Brown, Cai and DasGupta 2001 (dossier S8); scipy.stats.beta.ppf

methods.name: wilsonContinuity
methods.signature: wilsonContinuity(k: number, n: number, z = Z95): Interval
methods.definition: Wilson score interval with continuity correction (Newcombe 1998, method 4): lower = (2np + z^2 - 1 - z sqrt(z^2 - 2 - 1/n + 4p(n(1-p) + 1))) / (2(n + z^2)), upper = (2np + z^2 + 1 + z sqrt(z^2 + 2 - 1/n + 4p(n(1-p) - 1))) / (2(n + z^2)); lower 0 when k = 0, upper 1 when k = n; clipped to [0, 1]
methods.source: Newcombe 1998, Two-sided confidence intervals for the single proportion (dossier S8)

methods.name: newcombeDifference
methods.signature: newcombeDifference(k1: number, n1: number, k2: number, n2: number): Interval
methods.definition: Newcombe hybrid score interval for p1 - p2 of two independent rates (method 10): with Wilson bounds (l1, u1) and (l2, u2), lower = d - sqrt((p1 - l1)^2 + (u2 - p2)^2), upper = d + sqrt((u1 - p1)^2 + (p2 - l2)^2), d = p1 - p2
methods.source: Newcombe 1998, Interval estimation for the difference between independent proportions

methods.name: tInterval
methods.signature: tInterval(values: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Student's t interval for a mean: mean -/+ t(1 - alpha/2, n - 1) s / sqrt(n), s the sample standard deviation
methods.source: scipy.stats.t; the interval the dossier S22 (Adding error bars to evals) reports for a mean score

methods.name: poissonInterval
methods.signature: poissonInterval(count: number, exposure: number, alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Exact (Garwood) interval for a Poisson rate: chi2(alpha/2, 2c) / 2 and chi2(1 - alpha/2, 2c + 2) / 2, divided by the exposure; lower 0 when c = 0

methods.name: fisherExact
methods.signature: fisherExact(a: number, b: number, c: number, d: number): { oddsRatio: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Fisher's exact test on the 2x2 table [[a, b], [c, d]], two-sided p-value summing the tables no more likely than the observed one (relative tolerance 1e-7), sample odds ratio ad / bc

methods.name: welchTTest
methods.signature: welchTTest(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Welch's two-sample t test, two-sided, Welch-Satterthwaite degrees of freedom

methods.name: mannWhitneyU
methods.signature: mannWhitneyU(x: readonly number[], y: readonly number[]): { statistic: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Mann-Whitney U test, two-sided, normal approximation with the tie correction and the continuity correction; statistic is U of x (the number of pairs with x > y, ties counting 1/2)

methods.name: chiSquareIndependence
methods.signature: chiSquareIndependence(table: readonly (readonly number[])[]): { statistic: number; df: number; pValue: number }
methods.definition: Pearson's chi-square test of independence of an r x c table of counts, no continuity correction, df (r - 1)(c - 1)

methods.name: holm
methods.signature: holm(pvalues: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): { adjusted: number[]; rejected: boolean[] }
methods.definition: Holm step-down: sort ascending, adjusted p(i) = max over j <= i of min(1, (m - j + 1) p(j)), in input order; rejected when adjusted <= alpha

methods.name: bonferroni
methods.signature: bonferroni(pvalues: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): { adjusted: number[]; rejected: boolean[] }
methods.definition: Bonferroni: adjusted min(1, m p), rejected when adjusted <= alpha

methods.name: benjaminiYekutieli
methods.signature: benjaminiYekutieli(pvalues: readonly number[], q = 0.05): { adjusted: number[]; rejected: boolean[] }
methods.definition: Benjamini-Yekutieli: the Benjamini-Hochberg step-up with m replaced by m c(m), c(m) = sum over i of 1 / i; valid under any dependence

methods.name: sprtBernoulli
methods.signature: sprtBernoulli(input: { p0: number; p1: number; alpha: number; beta: number; outcomes: readonly (0 | 1)[] }): { decision: 'reject-null' | 'accept-null' | 'continue'; index: number; llr: number }
methods.definition: Wald's SPRT for a failure rate: log likelihood ratio summed over outcomes (1 a failure), reject H0 (rate p0) at the first index with llr >= ln((1 - beta) / alpha), accept at llr <= ln(beta / (1 - alpha)); index -1 and the final llr when neither boundary is met

methods.name: alphaSpending
methods.signature: alphaSpending(t: number, alpha: number, kind: 'obrien-fleming' | 'pocock'): number
methods.definition: Lan-DeMets spending functions, the cumulative alpha spent at information fraction t: O'Brien-Fleming type 2 - 2 Phi(z(1 - alpha/2) / sqrt(t)); Pocock type alpha ln(1 + (e - 1) t)
methods.source: Lan and DeMets 1983; group sequential tests (dossier S32)

methods.name: hoeffdingSampleSize
methods.signature: hoeffdingSampleSize(epsilon: number, delta: number): number
methods.definition: The distribution-free sample size for a rate within +/- epsilon with probability 1 - delta: ceil(ln(2 / delta) / (2 epsilon^2))
methods.source: Hoeffding's inequality (dossier S35, section 3.1: 738 for +/- 0.05 at 95 percent)

methods.name: normalSampleSize
methods.signature: normalSampleSize(p: number, epsilon: number, alpha = 0.05): number
methods.definition: The normal-approximation sample size for a rate p within +/- epsilon: ceil(z(1 - alpha/2)^2 p (1 - p) / epsilon^2)

methods.name: betaPosteriorBelow
methods.signature: betaPosteriorBelow(input: { failures: number; n: number; margin: number; priorA?: number; priorB?: number }): number
methods.definition: Bayesian stopping: the posterior probability that the failure rate is below the margin, Beta(priorA + failures, priorB + n - failures) cdf at the margin; prior Beta(1, 1) by default

methods.name: twoProportionSampleSize
methods.signature: twoProportionSampleSize(input: { p1: number; p2: number; alpha?: number; power?: number }): number
methods.definition: Units per group to detect p1 vs p2 with a two-sided two-proportion test (no continuity correction): ceil((z(1-alpha/2) sqrt(2 pbar (1 - pbar)) + z(power) sqrt(p1 q1 + p2 q2))^2 / (p1 - p2)^2); the inverse of mde

methods.name: shannonEntropy
methods.signature: shannonEntropy(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Plug-in Shannon entropy in nats, -sum p ln p over the classes with a count

methods.name: simpsonIndex
methods.signature: simpsonIndex(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Simpson concentration, sum of p^2 (plug-in)

methods.name: pielouEvenness
methods.signature: pielouEvenness(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Pielou evenness J = H / ln S, H the Shannon entropy in nats and S the classes with a count

methods.name: rarefiedRichness
methods.signature: rarefiedRichness(counts: readonly number[], m: number): number
methods.definition: Expected classes in a random subsample of m units without replacement: sum over classes of 1 - C(n - x_i, m) / C(n, m)
methods.source: Colwell, Chao and co-authors 2012; Chao and co-authors 2014 (dossier S24, S25)

methods.name: chao1Interval
methods.signature: chao1Interval(counts: readonly number[], alpha = 0.05): Interval
methods.definition: Chao1 with its log-normal interval (Chao 1987, with the bias factor k = (n - 1) / n as in EstimateS): var = f2 (k r^2 / 2 + k^2 r^3 + k^2 r^4 / 4), r = f1 / f2; T = Chao1 - S_obs; K = exp(z sqrt(ln(1 + var / T^2))); interval [S_obs + T / K, S_obs + T K]; estimate Chao1. Cases have f2 > 0
methods.source: Chao 1987, Estimating the population size for capture-recapture data with unequal catchability

methods.name: aceEstimator
methods.signature: aceEstimator(counts: readonly number[], rare = 10): number
methods.definition: Abundance-based coverage estimator (Chao and Lee 1992): classes with count <= rare are rare; C = 1 - f1 / N_rare; gamma^2 = max(S_rare / C * sum i (i - 1) f_i / (N_rare (N_rare - 1)) - 1, 0); ACE = S_abund + S_rare / C + f1 / C gamma^2
methods.source: Chao and Lee 1992; EstimateS user guide

methods.name: chaoShannon
methods.signature: chaoShannon(counts: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Chao, Wang and Jost 2013 entropy estimator: sum over classes of (x/n)(sum from k = x to n - 1 of 1/k), plus (f1/n)(1 - A)^(1 - n)(-ln A - sum from r = 1 to n - 1 of (1 - A)^r / r) with A = 2 f2 / ((n - 1) f1 + 2 f2) (when f2 = 0: A = 2 / ((n - 1)(f1 - 1) + 2); no second term when f1 = 0)
methods.source: Chao, Wang and Jost 2013, Entropy and the species accumulation curve (Methods in Ecology and Evolution)

methods.name: extrapolatedRichness
methods.signature: extrapolatedRichness(counts: readonly number[], extra: number): number
methods.definition: Expected classes after `extra` more units (Chao and co-authors 2014, equation 9): S_obs + f0 (1 - (1 - f1 / (n f0 + f1))^extra), f0 = ((n - 1)/n) f1^2 / (2 f2), or ((n - 1)/n) f1 (f1 - 1) / 2 when f2 = 0

methods.name: vendiScore
methods.signature: vendiScore(similarity: readonly (readonly number[])[]): number
methods.definition: Vendi score: exp(-sum lambda ln lambda) over the eigenvalues lambda of K / n, K a symmetric similarity matrix with ones on the diagonal (eigenvalues at or below 1e-15 left out)
methods.source: Friedman and Dieng, The Vendi Score (dossier S1)

methods.name: kishEffectiveSize
methods.signature: kishEffectiveSize(weights: readonly number[]): number
methods.definition: Kish's effective sample size of weighted units, (sum w)^2 / sum w^2
methods.source: Owen, Monte Carlo theory, chapter 9, equation 9.13 (dossier S43)

methods.name: stratifiedMean
methods.signature: stratifiedMean(input: { means: readonly number[]; sizes: readonly number[]; sds: readonly number[]; samples: readonly number[] }): { estimate: number; variance: number }
methods.definition: Stratified estimator of a mean: sum W_h ybar_h with W_h = N_h / N; variance sum W_h^2 (1 - n_h / N_h) s_h^2 / n_h (finite population correction)
methods.source: Stratified sampling (dossier S34); Cochran, Sampling Techniques, 5.4

methods.name: importanceWeights
methods.signature: importanceWeights(userShares: readonly number[], generatorShares: readonly number[]): number[]
methods.definition: The weight of each stratum when the generator over- or under-samples it: user share divided by generator share (the shares need not sum to 1; a zero generator share with a positive user share is a RangeError)

methods.name: clusteredStandardError
methods.signature: clusteredStandardError(values: readonly number[], clusters: readonly (string | number)[]): number
methods.definition: Standard error of a mean when values cluster (dossier S22, Adding error bars to evals, equation for clustered questions): sqrt(sum over clusters c of (sum over i in c of (x_i - xbar))^2) / n, no small-sample correction
methods.source: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals, arXiv 2411.00640 (dossier S22)

methods.name: pairedStandardError
methods.signature: pairedStandardError(a: readonly number[], b: readonly number[]): { difference: number; standardError: number }
methods.definition: Paired difference of two models on the same questions (dossier S22): difference mean(a - b), standard error sd(a - b) / sqrt(n) with the n - 1 sample standard deviation
methods.source: Miller 2024, Adding Error Bars to Evals (dossier S22)

methods.name: goelOkumoto
methods.signature: goelOkumoto(t: number, total: number, rate: number): { expected: number; intensity: number }
methods.definition: Goel-Okumoto reliability growth: expected failures by time t, m(t) = N (1 - e^(-phi t)), and the failure intensity N phi e^(-phi t)
methods.source: Pai 2002, A survey of software reliability models (dossier S26)

methods.name: goelOkumotoFit
methods.signature: goelOkumotoFit(failureTimes: readonly number[], observedUntil: number): { total: number; rate: number }
methods.definition: Maximum likelihood fit of the Goel-Okumoto model to failure times observed on [0, T]: phi solves k / phi - k T e^(-phi T) / (1 - e^(-phi T)) = sum t_i, then N = k / (1 - e^(-phi T))
